scopeDecisions.decision: Production parity of RTDB is claimed only for the recorded cases enumerated in the conditions: REST PUT/GET/PATCH of numbers, objects, arrays and priorities, format=export, orderBy with startAt/limitToFirst/limitToLast and their refusals, ETag and if-match, and the recorded validation errors; Security Rules loading (48 recorded M14 refusals) and owner/UID .read/.write evaluation with auth_variable_override and genuine email/password users; anonymous SSE put/patch/cancel; the web SDK over WebSocket and long polling for value listeners, onDisconnect set, remove, one compare-and-set transaction schedule and the genuine-Auth sign-in/sign-out/refresh/delete flow. The emulator-only Rules coverage view, import/export/reset/namespaces and the UI database view are compared with the official emulator or verified locally.
scopeDecisions.rationale: These are the shapes recorded on the sandbox; anything else served for RTDB follows the official emulator and is listed as unverified in R2.

scopeDecisions.decision: UNVERIFIED and outside this closure (not observed in production): reconnect/resume, child-event and query ordering across goOffline/goOnline, and query-scoped listener cancellation (CV08); REST POST/push ids, DELETE, server values (.sv timestamp and increment), shallow, print=silent, equalTo/endAt/startAfter/endBefore, $priority ordering, timeout and writeSizeLimit; Security Rules .validate, cascading, data/newData/root, query-based rules, auth.token claims and .indexOn enforcement texts beyond the recorded query; SDK child events, SDK queries, update/push and multi-location updates and SDK server values; onDisconnect register/cancel/re-register and a Rules change between registration and firing (CV10); RTDB-triggered Cloud Functions v1/v2 delivery (CV14, implemented locally but never observed in production); Firebase ID token expiry, tampered signatures, revocation, tenants and wrong-project tokens; latency, throughput, quotas, billing, multi-region and instance management APIs; Android, Apple, Unity and the Java/Python Admin SDKs (owner 1471 Q8); the Node Admin SDK beyond the official-emulator smokes in tools/sdk-smoke-database.
scopeDecisions.rationale: None of these was observed in production: the CV08/CV10 local gap actors never produced a result and no RTDB trigger was ever deployed (CV14). fireemu's behaviour there follows the official emulator and is provisional. Each needs its own production observation before it can join the closure.

integratedRegression.releaseBindingNote: The three comparisons were run on one local release build (RUSTC_WRAPPER empty, --locked) whose Rust sources equal origin/main 5a15d1631. The release job cannot rerun them yet (excluded kind rtdb-production-comparison-v1 in conformance/src/release-strict-regression.mjs): the replay tools need an installed-binary check and export-comparison mode, and two of them need Chromium. The residual comparison (production-5, CV08/CV10) is bound to its own release binary, built from origin/main 00abe06b4 (the multi-path order fix). The three older comparisons, which stay bound to the binary above, were re-run on an order-fixed build and reproduce row for row (review 2026-10-27, check 9): REST 120 MATCH and 4 KNOWN_DIFFERENCE with the same rows, M14 48/48, CV07 36/36 and CV11 with 0 differences.

restMemberOrder.statement: Two REST answers differ from production only in the member order of the JSON body, in both rounds: the PATCH answer for `{"y/z":"t","w":3}` (production keeps the request's order, fireemu answers in key order) and GET query.json?orderBy="h"&startAt=2 (production lists children in orderBy order, fireemu in key order). Status, parsed JSON and ETag are equal; the JS SDK parses both into the same snapshot.

longPollingIdleClose.statement: A long-polling client that goes offline without closing has its onDisconnect writes run when the server drops the idle connection: production after 99.3 s to 104.0 s in the four recorded flows (100.8 s and 104.0 s in the onDisconnect recording, 99.3 s and 103.2 s in production-5), fireemu after 104.3 s to about 105 s (100 s idle timeout plus the client's poll timing). The event sequence is identical; the comparison judges the delay within 5 s of production's range.

cv11WriteAfterDeleteRace.statement: After user A is deleted, the admin write's acknowledgement and the listener's value event race in both production and fireemu; the comparison judges the events of that step (and only that step) unordered; every other step, including the multi-event steps signin-a, signout, resignin-a and refresh-after-delete, is judged in recorded order. Transport request counts (long-polling HTTP requests per profile) and millisecond timings are not compared.

sseFraming.statement: Production sends event streams with Connection: close and closes the socket after the cancel event; fireemu uses chunked transfer encoding, ends the chunked body after cancel and keeps the connection. The event bytes are identical. Tracked in docs.local/issues/open/rtdb-sse-connection-close-framing.md.

googleSignedTokens.statement: Local RTDB accepts only ID tokens issued by fireemu's Auth (or the owner credential); production Google-signed tokens are not accepted locally, and strict refuses a non-owner gauth credential with production's permission_denied.

cv09LongPollingCells.statement: The committed CV09 test replays the WebSocket rows. The long-polling cells r1_lp and r2_lp carry the same request bodies inside long-polling envelopes; they were matched cell by cell only by the private local CAS harness on source 72f67f1f (binary 8509f53a), which is not rerun on the closure binary.

browserRunsOnOlderBinaries.statement: The browser runs of the Rules coverage view (attempt 7 on 51a089e2) and of the UI database view (fb6faccc5, rebound on df744e06) were not rerun on the closure binary; the committed nextest and ui unit tests of both surfaces pass on the closure commit.

onDisconnectPrioritizedSplit.statement: Not claimed: an onDisconnect value that carries `.priority`, followed by a cancel of one of its children (not of the priority itself). The official emulator accepts every request and then drops the whole disconnect update (no frame, the data stays null, even a write registered next to it); production was not observed; fireemu fires the remaining children. Tracked in docs.local/issues/open/rtdb-ondisconnect-split-of-a-prioritized-value-drops-the-whole-update.md.
